svg.text: Opening the surface is the act of whichever surface
offers it, and the board draws it (BP11); this process
starts inside it. The batch a previous gesture left staged
is in front of the user when capture opens - it survives
leaving the gesture, a crash and a restart, so capture
resumes it rather than starting over. Where nothing was
left staged, the batch starts empty.
Closing the surface is not discarding the batch: it
survives as a draft, and nothing it describes takes effect
until it is committed. Throwing it away is the discard act.
Staging is one task at a time, and the batch is what has
been staged so far. Staging is also what sets the priority:
the batch is laid out as three priority columns - Important
and Urgent, Not Important and Urgent, Important and
Not Urgent - and the column a task is staged into is the
What a staged task says and the priority it carries are
fields of the one request, which is why moving it into
another priority column arrives here too: the editor and
the drag are two gestures on one request. Nothing takes
effect until the batch is committed.
A staged task owns nothing, so there is nothing to
disclose and no cascade to approve. Throwing one away
and throwing the whole batch away are two gestures on
A staged task is not a commit. It is kept outside version
Every task in the batch lands on the board capture was
opened from - a project's board, or Chores where that is
the board the user is on. Capture names no board and
creates none. The batch commits as one act.
A staged task is never on a board, so its priority is open
for as long as the batch is uncommitted.
fix what a staged task says
